questions.question: What is the key distinction between the Arabic words 'Ahad' and 'Wahid' as used in this surah?
options: They are completely interchangeable terms with no difference in meaning
Wahid denotes numerical singularity while Ahad carries the additional force of absolute indivisibility, with no partner or counterpart even imaginable
Ahad means the first while Wahid means the only
Wahid is reserved exclusively for Allah while Ahad can apply to anything
questions.explanation: The layer 1 tafsir explains that while both words mean 'one', Wahid simply denotes a numerical singular whereas Ahad negates the very concept of a partner, component, or counterpart. No created thing can be called Ahad in this absolute sense; the word belongs exclusively to Allah.

questions.question: True or false: According to an authentic narration in Sahih Bukhari, the Prophet stated that Surah Al-Ikhlas equals one third of the Quran.
questions.explanation: The layer 1 tafsir cites this authenticated narration in Sahih Bukhari. Scholars explain it by noting that the Quran addresses three broad themes - theology, legal rulings, and accounts of history - and this surah comprises the entirety of the first category.

questions.question: Which of the following best captures the meaning of 'Al-Samad' as explained in the foundational tafsir?
options: The Most Merciful who forgives all sins without condition
The One to whom all needs are directed, who is utterly self-sufficient and complete with no need of anything
The Creator who originated the heavens and the earth in six days
The Hidden One whose nature can never be known by any creature
questions.explanation: Layer 1 explains that Al-Samad refers to the One to whom all needs and requests are directed, while He neither requires nor lacks anything. Hasan al-Basri and Qatadah further understood it as One who is utterly solid and complete, with no hollow or void within.

questions.question: True or false: Imam Tabari records via Ubayy ibn Kab that this surah was revealed when polytheists asked the Prophet to describe the lineage and ancestry of his Lord.
questions.explanation: Layer 2 cites Tabari in Jami al-Bayan recording this report through Ubayy ibn Kab as the most prominent occasion of revelation. The surah was revealed in its entirety as the response, and similar reports mention People of the Scripture posing comparable theological challenges.

questions.question: How did Ibn Abbas, as recorded by Imam Tabari, describe Al-Samad?
options: The One who created Adam from clay and breathed His spirit into him
The chieftain whose chieftaincy is perfect, the most noble whose nobility is perfect, and the all-knowing whose knowledge is perfect
The One who sees but is not seen, who hears but is not heard
The Master of the Day of Judgment who weighs all deeds in the balance
questions.explanation: Layer 2 records Tabari's transmission from Ibn Abbas describing Al-Samad as 'the chieftain whose chieftaincy is perfect, the most noble whose nobility is perfect, the most forbearing whose forbearance is perfect, the all-knowing whose knowledge is perfect, the most wise whose wisdom is perfect - and He is Allah, may His glory be exalted.'

questions.question: True or false: Sayyid Qutb argued in Fi Zilal al-Quran that these four verses together constitute the most complete and condensed articulation of pure monotheism in human language.
questions.explanation: Layer 3 cites Sayyid Qutb closing his commentary on this surah by reflecting that read together, these four verses constitute the most complete and condensed articulation of pure monotheism in human language, offering spiritual freedom from every false absolute.

questions.question: According to Wahbah al-Zuhayli, what is the role of verse 3 ('He neither begets nor is born') in interfaith dialogue?
options: It denies the prophethood of Jesus and rejects all of Christian teaching
It represents the Quran's respectful yet unequivocal position on the core theological differences between Islam and Christianity, while still affirming Jesus as a great messenger
It commands Muslims to avoid all theological discussion with Christians and Jews
It establishes that Allah may have spiritual children but not biological ones
questions.explanation: Layer 3 cites al-Zuhayli situating this verse within its interfaith dialogue context. The Islamic position does not deny the prophethood of Jesus - the Quran affirms him as a great messenger - but firmly separates the concept of Allah from any form of paternal relationship with created beings.
